title: Two Coworkers Talk About a Stressful Week
script: Dewi: [warmly] Fajar, I don't think I can survive another week like this one. Three deadlines, all in the same week.
Fajar: I saw your calendar. It looked completely full, honestly. How are you holding up?
Dewi: [honestly] Not great. I stayed until nine last night, and I still didn't finish the report.
Fajar: Did you tell our manager the workload is too much right now?
Dewi: [thoughtful] Not yet. I don't want to seem like I can't handle my job.
Fajar: Asking for help isn't the same as failing, Dewi. Everyone on this team is drowning this week.
Dewi: [carefully] Maybe you're right. I keep thinking I should just push through it alone.
Fajar: I talked to our manager yesterday about my own deadline. She moved it back two days without any problem.
Dewi: [reflective] Really? I didn't know that was even an option.
Fajar: It usually is, if you explain it calmly and early, before everything becomes urgent and messy.
Dewi: [practically] Okay, I'll talk to her this afternoon. What exactly did you say to her?
Fajar: I just said I had three big tasks and needed help deciding which one truly mattered most this week.
Dewi: [calmly] That sounds much better than what I was planning, which was just complaining loudly.
Fajar: Complaining feels good for a minute, but it doesn't move any deadlines.
Dewi: [encouraging] Fair point. I also haven't eaten a proper lunch in four days.
Fajar: That explains why you look so tired. Come eat with me now, before this conversation continues.
Dewi: Actually, yes. I think I forgot that taking a break is allowed.
Fajar: [warmly] We all forget that sometimes. Let's go, and then you can plan what to say to our manager.
Dewi: Thanks, Fajar. I feel a little less alone with all of this now.
Fajar: That's what coworkers are for. We're in this messy week together.
